data.summary: The 16‑week plan builds a solid foundation in Limits (the student’s weak unit) early, then progresses through differentiation, integration, and differential equations while interleaving practice and review. Each week stays within the 5‑hour limit, includes concrete tasks, and reserves the final two weeks for mixed review and timed practice.

weeks.focus: Introduce limits and practice estimating them
tasks: Read the textbook sections for 1.1‑1.4 and take concise notes.
Do 10 limit‑value estimation problems from graphs (1.3) and 10 from tables (1.4).
Complete 5 algebraic limit problems (1.5) and check answers with the solution guide.

weeks.focus: Deepen limit concepts and join live class
tasks: Attend live class 10800 and actively participate in the limit examples.
After class, redo the class’s example problems for 1.1‑1.3.
Solve 8 practice problems on defining average and instantaneous rates (2.1).
Write derivative definitions for 5 functions (2.2) and verify with calculator.
Estimate derivatives at 10 points using difference quotients (2.3).
Complete a worksheet connecting differentiability and continuity (2.4).
Practice the Power Rule on 15 polynomial functions (2.5).
Watch a tutorial on the Chain Rule and do 12 chain‑rule problems (3.1).
Do 8 implicit differentiation problems (3.2) and check each step against the solution key.
Derive formulas for the derivatives of inverse functions (3.3) for 5 examples.
Complete 10 problems differentiating inverse trigonometric functions (3.4).
Write a short explanation of the derivative’s meaning in context (4.1).
Solve 6 straight‑line motion problems connecting position, velocity, and acceleration (4.2).

weeks.focus: Rates of change and related rates
tasks: Complete 8 applied‑rate‑of‑change problems (4.3).
Work through 5 related‑rates scenarios (4.4), showing all setup steps.

weeks.focus: Mean Value and Extreme Value Theorems
tasks: Prove the Mean Value Theorem for 3 functions (5.1).
Identify critical points and classify them using the Extreme Value Theorem for 6 functions (5.2).
Determine intervals of increase/decrease for 8 functions (5.3).
Apply the First Derivative Test to find local extrema for 6 functions (5.4).
Explore 4 accumulation scenarios and describe them verbally (6.1).
Compute left, right, and midpoint Riemann sums for 5 regions (6.2).
Write the summation notation for each Riemann sum and evaluate (6.3).
Prove the FTC for 2 functions and use it to evaluate 8 definite integrals (6.4).
Create a one‑page cheat sheet linking accumulation functions to antiderivatives.
Set up differential equations for 5 real‑world situations (7.1).
Verify solutions for those equations using substitution (7.2).
Sketch slope fields for 4 differential equations (7.3).
Answer reasoning questions about solution behavior from the slope fields (7.4).
Calculate the average value of 6 functions on given intervals (8.1).
Use integrals to find position, velocity, and acceleration for 4 motion problems (8.2).

weeks.focus: Mixed integration review and area between curves
tasks: Solve 5 applied‑context accumulation problems (8.3).
Find the area between curves for 6 pairs of functions (8.4).
Take a full‑length timed practice exam (all units).
Review every incorrect answer, writing a brief explanation of the error.
Do a final 20‑question mixed‑topic drill focusing on weak spots (limits, related rates).

data.final_week_advice: In the last week, simulate exam conditions, focus on speed and accuracy, and use the error‑analysis sheet to fix lingering misconceptions. Rest well the night before the exam and trust the systematic practice you’ve built.
